Enter/Queue while the agent works queues the message on the host (Conversation.queuedMessages, in memory, broadcast like status; ConversationService.send replaces deliverAsNextMessage, so canvas next-message answers use the same queue). Queue panel above the composer: Edit pulls a message back into the composer (joined with any draft), ↑ in an empty composer pulls the last one, Remove drops it; each queued message goes out when the previous turn ends, also after Stop (assumption: stopping is how you redirect). Protocol: conversation.queue.edit/remove. e2e: opencode queue test (queue 2, ↑, Edit, Remove, answer the ask, edited text sent as next turn).

When the conversation's Claude settings (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR from its profile env, else ~/.claude) have statusLine.type=command, the host (host/statusline.ts) runs it like Claude Code: sh -c in the workspace dir, detached (no controlling tty), Claude-Code-compatible JSON on stdin, profile env + COLUMNS/TERM, 5 s cap, output taken at exit (a disowned background job holding stdout does not block). xterm.js renders the ANSI; the terminal grows to show wrapped rows. Refresh on conversation change + every 30 s. Toggle Built-in / Your statusline (localStorage, per browser). Unattended assumptions: a configured Claude statusLine is used by default (the toggle switches back); it also runs for opencode conversations; total_duration_ms counts from conversation creation; current_usage puts all used tokens in input_tokens. Each turn's snapshot is now its own commit with its own ref (refs/mirador/turns/<workspace>/<time>-<commit>); each write keeps the newest 100 and drops the rest, and git's own gc then frees what only they held. The old chain ref moves over as one snapshot and ages out the same way. A restore counts changed submodules apart and says it leaves them as they are; a turn whose files git dropped says Mirador no longer keeps them.
